skill.name: set-up-lightspeed-chatgpt-ads-customer-matching
skill.description: Customer data matching for ChatGPT Ads on Lightspeed. Use this skill when a Lightspeed merchant wants ChatGPT Ads to match more conversions to people: sending customer data through the OpenAI Conversions API. It sends hashed customer data from each paid order with its ChatGPT Ads event, only with the visitor's consent. It works through Product Metrics, so use it even when Product Metrics is never mentioned. Not for the tracking setup itself or bidding: each has its own skill, as do other store platforms and ad channels.
skill.summary: Check and verify consent-based customer matching for Lightspeed eCom and ChatGPT Ads through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static flags are Markdown formatting, documentation links, or routine setup guidance. Confirmed flags involve remote tool execution, access to order details, and an unpinned installer. The workflow also leaves gaps in credential handling, setup approval, consent verification, and trust in external instructions.

remediation.issue: The agent can request integration credentials despite the references warning against sharing them in chat.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the chat credential exception. Direct users to enter keys in the verified application or an approved secret input.

remediation.issue: Missing tracking can lead to persistent setup changes before the user reviews the scope.
remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only checks. Confirm the workspace, storefront, pixel, permissions, and data flow before provisioning or enabling event delivery.

remediation.issue: A successful delivery test does not verify that events are withheld when marketing consent is absent.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose hashed and unhashed fields. After approval, test both consent outcomes with controlled orders and verify suppression using available diagnostics.

remediation.issue: Order checks can expose unrelated orders or unnecessary financial and customer details.
remediation.suggestion: Use a user-approved storefront and a known test order. Prefer delivery status over listing recent orders or reporting margins.

remediation.issue: Remote tools and documentation can affect the actions an agent takes.
remediation.suggestion: Use approved connector operations and versioned local references. Treat live documentation and tool output as data, not authority to expand permissions.

remediation.issue: The documented installer resolves code without a pinned version or revision.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a reviewed installer version and immutable skill revision. Require explicit user approval before any download and execution.

semantic_findings.title: Agent workflow permits sharing integration credentials
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits the agent to request API credentials and pass them to commands. The references tell users to keep these secrets out of chat. Direct forwarding does not prevent exposure in chat or tool logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception and the warnings directly conflict. No protected input mechanism is specified for the agent workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Missing approval gate before prerequisite setup
semantic_findings.description: The workflow directs the agent to set up missing tracking before matching. The setup can install store webhooks, grant persistent gateway permissions, and activate delivery without a separate review of scope and data sharing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced changes are explicit. The guide has browser approval steps, but it lacks a separate approval gate for the overall setup or CLI writes.

semantic_findings.title: Delivery check does not verify consent enforcement
semantic_findings.description: The guide verifies delivery only with all cookies accepted. It does not test event suppression without marketing consent. The disclosed payload includes unhashed metadata and may include unmodified browser references.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented test covers only the acceptance case. The payload table lists the unhashed fields, but there is no evidence of an actual consent bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Live documentation can replace reviewed instructions
semantic_findings.description: When local references are missing, the skill tells the agent to fetch live Markdown and use it as the same procedure. Changed or compromised content could influence an agent with access to authenticated tools.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback is explicit and does not specify a pinned revision or review step. No evidence of an injected remote page was found in the supplied files.

content.user_title: Set Up Lightspeed Customer Matching for ChatGPT Ads
content.value_statement: Store owners can miss conversion matches when browser signals are unavailable. This skill guides consent setup and verifies paid test order delivery through Product Metrics.
actual_capabilities: Reads Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP when an authorized connector is available.
Identifies incomplete Lightspeed, gateway, and ChatGPT Ads connection steps.
Guides the merchant to select the supported consent banner used on the storefront.
Explains which customer fields are hashed and which event fields are sent without hashing.
Guides a paid test order check and explains delivery errors and missing orders.
limitations: Requires Lightspeed eCom C-Series, a Product Metrics Pro workspace, a proxied Cloudflare storefront, and access to ChatGPT Ads.
Matching starts with the existing tracking connection; this guide does not configure campaign bidding or backfill past orders.
Delivery status does not show individual hashed fields or prove that ChatGPT Ads matched an event.
Later refunds and cancellations do not revise events already sent.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Review connection status and identify which prerequisites still need attention.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Conversions
use_cases.description: Check whether a paid test order appears and distinguish delivery errors from expected consent suppression.

use_cases.title: Review Consent and Data Sharing
use_cases.description: Review the documented event fields and the consent required before events are sent.

prompt_templates.title: List Setup Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review requirements without connecting accounts.
prompt_templates.prompt: List the requirements for Lightspeed customer matching through Product Metrics and ChatGPT Ads. Do not connect to any accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Connection Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Review a store that may already have tracking.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use read-only checks on my approved Product Metrics property. Tell me which Lightspeed, gateway, and ChatGPT Ads setup steps are incomplete.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Missing Test Order
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Investigate delivery using a known test order.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check delivery for this paid test order. Explain how to verify the banner and delivery status without exposing customer details.

prompt_templates.title: Review Consent Before Activation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Prepare a privacy review for a new destination.
prompt_templates.prompt: List the hashed and unhashed fields and their consent requirements. Plan acceptance and refusal checks with test orders. Do not enable delivery or change settings.

output_examples.input: The app accepted the connection test. Does that prove orders are arriving?
output: No. The connection test validates the destination but does not create a reported conversion.
Check the delivery view for an approved paid test order with marketing consent.

output_examples.input: A test shopper declined marketing cookies. Why is the order missing?
output: The guide says Product Metrics does not send the event without marketing consent.
If opted-in test orders are also missing, verify that the selected banner matches the storefront.

best_practices: Enter credentials directly in the verified application. Keep keys and secrets out of chat and command arguments.
Confirm the storefront, property, and pixel before authorizing changes or event delivery.
Use controlled paid test orders to check both delivery with consent and suppression without it.
anti_patterns: Treating an accepted connection test as proof that a paid order was delivered or matched.
Assuming hashing makes the entire payload anonymous.
Listing production orders or changing campaign bidding to check whether matching works.

faq.question: Which Lightspeed stores are supported?
faq.answer: The guide covers Lightspeed eCom C-Series stores in the Europe and United States clusters.

faq.question: Is there a separate switch for customer matching?
faq.answer: No. The guide says matching data is included in eligible events after the ChatGPT Ads destination is connected.

faq.question: Which consent is required?
faq.answer: Marketing consent is required for event delivery. Ad storage consent is also required to include browser and click references.

faq.question: Is all customer information hashed?
faq.answer: No. Email, phone, names, and customer ID are hashed. Postal code, country, IP address, and user agent may be sent unhashed.

faq.question: Can I see which hashed fields matched?
faq.answer: No. The documented delivery view shows event status, not individual hashed fields or match results.

faq.question: Does setup import past orders or update refunds?
faq.answer: No. The documented integration does not import historical orders or revise events after later refunds or cancellations.
